howto.name: Add your videos
howto.text: Drop or pick MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV, AVI or M4V files; the queue holds up to 25. This tool accepts files up to 200 MB each.

howto.name: Press Mute Video
howto.text: Each file is uploaded over HTTPS in turn, and FFmpeg on the PrivaTools server copies the video stream unchanged while leaving out every audio track.

howto.name: Download the silent video
howto.text: A single file downloads when it is ready, named after the original with _muted.mp4 at the end, so interview.mov becomes interview_muted.mp4; several can be saved one by one or together as mute-video-results.zip.

howto.name: Keep the sound separately
howto.text: Muting does not return the removed audio. If you want the soundtrack as its own file, run the original video through Extract Audio from Video as well.

faq.q: Is the picture changed at all?
faq.a: No. The video stream is copied without re-encoding, so the resolution, frame rate, codec and quality stay as they were, and so does the rotation that makes a portrait phone clip play upright. The container is rewritten without the audio, and one other change can happen: a text subtitle track kept in an MKV file is re-encoded to ASS, so SRT subtitles come back as ASS.

faq.q: Does the muted video keep where it was recorded?
faq.a: No. The location (GPS), the make, model and software of the phone or camera, the recording date, and tags such as the title and comments are left out. Chapter markers keep their place and titles, and a subtitle track kept in an MKV or WebM keeps its language.

faq.q: What format is the muted file?
faq.a: The same container you uploaded: an MKV comes back as Matroska, a WebM as WebM and an AVI as AVI, with the original video codec inside. The download name always ends in .mp4, though, so a muted holiday.mkv arrives as holiday_muted.mp4 with Matroska inside; rename it to .mkv if your player or editor goes by the extension. Nothing is converted; use Video Converter if you also need another format.

Every audio track, including commentary and extra languages. FFmpeg keeps one video stream, and in MKV and WebM files it can also carry over one text subtitle track. The removed audio cannot be recovered from the muted file.

faq.q: How much smaller will the file be?
faq.a: Smaller by roughly the size of the audio, which depends on its bitrate and length; the video portion is unchanged. A clip with a short or low-bitrate soundtrack barely shrinks.

faq.q: Can I replace the sound with a silent track?
faq.a: No. The audio is removed entirely rather than replaced with silence. A video without an audio track simply plays without sound.

faq.q: What if my file has no audio, or no video?
faq.a: A file without sound is still processed and comes back as a copy of the video. A file without a video stream, such as an audio-only recording saved with a video extension, fails with "Processing failed. Please try again."

Keep each file under 200 MB. From 200 MB to 500 MB the server refuses it with "File is too big for the server. Try compressing it first." A file over 500 MB is not added to the queue. FFmpeg has 180 seconds per file, after which the page says the server took too long, and the route is rate-limited at 5 requests a minute per IP address. Copying a stream needs no encoding, so it is much quicker than a conversion.

faq.q: What happens to my video on the server?
faq.a: It is uploaded over HTTPS and processed by FFmpeg on the PrivaTools server in isolated temporary per-request storage, not by a third-party service. Response cleanup removes the original and the muted copy after your download is sent, and a background sweep every five minutes clears leftovers older than ten minutes.
